answer.evidence: Rows 1-10 form a tyre-top ellipse. The width profile goes 9, 11, 13, 15 over rows 1-4, then stays at 15 through the hole rows 4-6, dips to 13 at row 7 and returns to 15 at rows 8-11, so the rim is rounded at the back and front. The hole (dark, rows 4-6 at x=8) sits inside a lighter ring, which reads as an open top seen from above. Row 11 is a dark front-edge line (#091125). Below it, rows 12-14 are the tread side at width 16, and row 15 is the dark bottom outline. That gives a 10-row top and a front face of about 4 rows, so the object reads as a 3/4 view cylinder.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny grey stack of tyres, about one tile in size, with a dark hole and a few stacked bands. It has only 6 raw colours and 5 visible tones per tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. The tyre rings look like 2-3 grey steps plus a dark outline, so the shading is shallow next to the 5-6 steps on the well and stall. The 0% neutral dark edge share suggests a tinted outline, but at this size the dark edges read as a uniform dark line around each ring, a sticker look rather than separation by value. There are no visible rubber grain dots, wear marks, scuffs or per-tyre highlights, so texture is flat. The 0% near-flat figure comes from the tiny silhouette, not from real texture. Next to the well and stall it looks thinner and flatter, so I fail it on density and texture.
